column1: # NFTBan — UNRESOLVED unbounded ownership/mode mutation sites
# Consumed by BOTH existing guards — tools/check-recursive-permissions.sh (pre-commit) and
# check_recursive_permissions() in .github/ci/health_check.sh (CI). There is no third guard.
# THIS IS NOT AN ALLOWLIST. A row means STILL WRONG, deliberately deferred, with a named
# owner decision. Rows are printed on every run so the debt stays visible, the count may
# only DECREASE, and a site that is NOT listed fails the build immediately.
# 2026-08-30 — LIST IS NOW EMPTY. OPEN_DEBT GO FALLBACK PARITY is CLOSED.
# LogDir (:89) was retired 2026-08-09. The remaining five were retired 2026-08-30:
# internal/installer/fhs/permissions.go::applyPermissions no longer maintains its own
# recursive ownership logic. Every tree now derives from RequiredDirs — the same canonical
# authority EnsureDirectories uses and that build/fhs-spec.yaml generates — via
# applyCanonicalTree(), which is bounded by that declaration and never recursive.
#   INVARIANT: RECOVERY/FALLBACK MUST NOT BE WEAKER THAN PRIMARY.  <- now satisfied.
# Two of the five were proven to violate the canonical matrix, not merely to be
# stylistically unbounded:
#   DataDir  chown -R nftban:nftban /var/lib/nftban  flattened reports/auditors
#            (root:nftban-auditor 0770/0660 — the audit-evidence boundary), plus backup/,
#            update-backups/ and pro/ (root:nftban). The PRIMARY generated script
#            explicitly excludes the auditor tree and re-applies it separately, so the
#            fallback was strictly weaker than the path it stands in for.
#   RunDir   chown -R nftban:nftban /run/nftban  flattened firewall-validate root:nftban 2750.
# The other three (EtcDir, BinDir, CacheDir) were owner/group-homogeneous per the matrix,
# so they diverged from no declared value; they were still unbounded across mount
# boundaries and are now bounded too.
# Measured behaviour, recorded so it is not re-derived as folklore:
#   symlinks   chown -R defaults to -P: it neither traverses symlinked dirs nor
#              dereferences symlinked files. NOT a vector. Adding -L or -H would be a
#              security change.
#   mounts     chown -R DOES cross bind mounts and mutates the real backing content.
#              chown has no --one-file-system; only find has -xdev.
